text:
A: Hiya. Can you hear me alright?
B: Hi, yeah, I can. Sorry, I'm Sana.
A: Liam. Er, I'm in Doncaster.
B: I'm in Luton. Erm, I've never really been up north. Only Birmingham, to my cousin's.
A: Birmingham's not really north, to be fair. Don't tell them I said that, mind.
B: I won't! Is that a football picture behind you?
A: Yeah, Doncaster Rovers. Me team. They're not very good at the minute, sorry.
B: That's okay, I don't really know football. My son watches it with my brother sometimes. Is that a PlayStation controller on the sofa?
A: Yeah, I play FIFA. Well, they call it EA FC now. I'm on nights, stacking shelves, so I get in about seven in the morning and have an hour on it before bed. Sort of helps me wind down, you know. Otherwise I just lie there with me head still going.
B: Oh, I get that. Not the nights, but lying there with your head going. Zayan would love you though. He's always asking me to play games and I'm so bad at them.
A: How old is he?
B: Five. He's in Year One. I saw your blanket on the sofa and I thought, oh, that's like mine. Same grey sofa as well.
A: Ha, everyone's got that sofa. What do you do, then?
B: I'm a kitchen assistant at a primary school. So I do the veg, serve the dinners, wash up. Today was jacket potatoes and beans, and half of them just ate the cheese off the top.
A: Sounds like my tea, that. Oven chips, sausages, beans. Every day, near enough. I get reduced stuff from work an' all, end of the shift. Sandwiches for like twenty pence.
B: Twenty pence? Seriously?
A: Sometimes, yeah. If you're there at the right time. It helps, do you know what I mean, cos money's a bit tight.
B: No, totally. Everything's gone up. School shoes, I nearly cried in the shop. Erm, sorry, that's a bit much.
A: No, it's not. Me mam says the same about everything. I go to hers for Sunday dinner most weeks. That's me proper meal.
B: Aw. I'm close with my mum as well. She lives ten minutes away and does Zayan's pick-up when my shift runs over. I'd be lost without her, honestly.
A: Yeah. Mine's fifteen minutes. It's nice having them close.
B: What do you do when you're not working? Just the FIFA?
A: Fishing, mostly. Ponds, canal. On me own usually. It's quiet. People think it's boring.
B: I don't think it's boring. It sounds kind of peaceful. I do henna, for weddings and Eid, and it's a bit like that. You just concentrate and everything else goes.
A: Henna, like on your hands?
B: Yeah, the patterns. I've got an Instagram for it but I never post. I'm too shy.
A: Same. I've got Facebook and I've not put owt on it in about three years. Er... so, I don't really know what else to ask, sorry.
B: No, it's fine! I'm the same. I think we've done really well, to be honest.
A: Yeah. I think it's about time anyway. It were nice talking to you, Sana.
B: You too, Liam. Hope your team wins.
